Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who bills what in Livonia

  • Livonia Assessment Department handles assessment.

Due dates

Search excerpt: bills mailed July 1 and Dec 1; winter payable without penalty through Feb 14. Summer due date not confirmed.. See the official page.

Local notes

Behind on Livonia property tax?
We buy Livonia houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Livonia by the numbers

Who bills and collects property tax in Livonia, Michigan?

The City of Livonia assesses and bills its own property tax, and Wayne County steps in only after a bill goes delinquent. The Assessment Department sets values and handles exemption forms. The Treasurer's Office, on the first floor of City Hall at 33000 Civic Center Drive, mails real and personal property tax bills on July 1 and December 1 and collects the payments.

Those payments are split among several taxing bodies listed by the city: the City of Livonia, Livonia Public Schools, Clarenceville Public Schools, Schoolcraft College, the State of Michigan education tax, Wayne County, Wayne County RESA and Oakland ISD. A house in the northeast corner of the city that falls in the Clarenceville district therefore carries a different mix of levies than one in the Livonia Public Schools territory.

  • Treasurer, bills, due dates, deferrals, special assessments, millage questions: (734) 466-2245.
  • Assessment Department, valuation and exemption forms: (734) 466-2220.
  • Water account: (734) 466-2278.
  • Inspection, for outstanding permits, violations, vacant or abandoned property registration fees and certificate of occupancy: (734) 466-2580.

When are Livonia property taxes due?

Summer taxes are billed July 1 and due September 14. Winter taxes are billed December 1 and due February 14. When a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day. Checks go to City of Livonia, Treasurer, 33000 Civic Center Drive, Livonia, MI 48154.

Livonia tax bill calendar and city fees
ItemRule
Summer billBilled July 1, due September 14
Winter billBilled December 1, due February 14
Returned payment$25 charge
Payment by a title, mortgage or servicing company without the original bill$5 duplicate bill fee
Unpaid real property tax after the city periodTurned over to the Wayne County Treasurer

The city says printouts or screenshots from its online system do not count as an original tax bill. A title company closing a Livonia sale should bring the original, or the $5 fee applies. Delinquent personal property tax stays with the city treasurer, while delinquent real property tax moves to the county.

How can I look up a Livonia tax bill and special assessments?

The city runs an online property inquiry system at livoniatax.org, using BS&A software. Agree to the disclaimer, search by address, and enter only the street name without Road, Street or Avenue, or just the house number. Click the property, open the Tax Information tab, and the taxes appear by year and season, with a detailed breakdown behind each year.

The city warns that errors on the site do not cancel taxes or special assessments owed, that the official records at City Hall cover current-year collections only, and that payments on delinquent taxes do not show online. To check a delinquent balance, contact the Wayne County Treasurer.

Special assessments are a separate item. Email specials@livonia.gov to request the status on a parcel. Vacant and abandoned property fees, permit issues and violations do not appear in the online system, so a seller who wants a clean closing should ask Inspection for those directly.

What exemptions and deferrals apply to a Livonia home?

The Assessment Department reminds homeowners of the principal residence exemption deadlines. An affidavit filed on or before June 1 earns the exemption on that year's summer and winter levy and later years while the home remains the owner's principal residence. One filed after June 1 and on or before November 1 applies to the current winter levy and later levies.

The city also publishes a form letting a homeowner defer the due date of winter taxes on a principal residence without penalty or interest, for a stated period set each year. Ask the Treasurer's Office which year's form and deadline applies. Wayne County adds that the poverty exemption is reached through the local assessing unit, so Livonia owners facing hardship should start with the Assessment Department, not the county.

Religious, charitable and educational exemption forms, plus personal property forms, are on the Assessment Department page, which accepts forms by email, mail or the City Hall drop box on the east side of the building.

What happens if Livonia property taxes go unpaid?

Unpaid summer and winter bills are forwarded to the Wayne County Treasurer. Wayne County lays out the state timeline this way: on March 1 unpaid taxes become delinquent at the county, adding a 4 percent administration fee and 1 percent interest per month. A $15 collection fee follows on October 1. The next March 1 the parcel forfeits to the county treasurer, with a $175 fee and recording fees, and interest rises to 1.5 percent per month retroactive to the first delinquency.

Foreclosure follows. Michigan's three-year process ends with the circuit court entering a judgment, and unpaid taxes on March 31 of the third year mean the owner loses the property. Wayne County sends at least ten notices before that point.

Owners with a financial hardship can apply for a Wayne County payment plan. Standards cited are 125 percent of the federal poverty level, and the application needs photo ID, a copy of the deed, proof of occupancy and proof of income. After a foreclosure, the former owner can claim remaining auction proceeds by filing a notice of intent by July 1 of that year.

What does it mean to sell a house in Livonia with tax due?

Livonia is a Wayne County city of about 95,500 people at the 2020 census, set roughly 20 miles northwest of downtown Detroit. It covers about 35.7 square miles of land, was organized as Livonia Township in 1835 and became a city in 1950. More than 40,000 housing units were counted in 2020, and only 2.7 percent were vacant. Ford, Trinity Health, Livonia Public Schools and St. Mary Mercy Hospital rank among the largest employers. Newburgh and Nankin lakes lie in the south and southwest, Hines Drive links them, and the Rosedale Gardens Historic District and the Laurel Park Place mall at Six Mile and Newburgh roads are among the places buyers know. The median age at the 2020 census was 45.6, and many homes here have been owned for decades, so a long-held house often has a taxable value well below its market value, a gap that closes for the next owner after a sale.

Most Livonia homes sold with tax due close like any other: the title company gets a payoff, pays the city or county from the seller's proceeds, and records the deed. If the bill is delinquent, ask Wayne County for the payoff figure, since City Hall no longer holds the balance. Owners behind on taxes, with an inherited house or a place that needs work, can ask for a cash offer and have the payoff settled at the table.

More questions about Livonia, MI Property Tax Guide

When is the Livonia summer tax due?

September 14. The summer bill is mailed July 1, and if September 14 lands on a weekend or holiday the due date becomes the next business day.

Where do I pay Livonia winter taxes?

Mail a check payable to the City of Livonia to Treasurer, 33000 Civic Center Drive, Livonia, MI 48154, or use the Treasurer's Office on the first floor of City Hall. Winter bills are due February 14.

Who do I call about a delinquent Livonia tax bill?

The Wayne County Treasurer. Delinquent real property taxes are turned over to the county, and the city's own records show current-year collections only.

How do I get the principal residence exemption in Livonia?

File the affidavit with the Assessment Department. Filing by June 1 covers that year's summer and winter taxes, and filing after June 1 through November 1 covers the winter levy.

Which school districts tax Livonia homes?

Livonia Public Schools serves most of the city, and a portion of the northeast is in Clarenceville Public Schools. Both appear among the bodies that receive the city's collections.
